 JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed under Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death caused in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioners in the nutshell is that, on 27.09.2023 at about 11.30 a.m, when the deceased was proceeding in his motorcycle bearing Reg.No.AP-39-HL-0113 slowly and cautiously on the left side of the Gowribidanur - Gudibande SH-94 road, when he reached near Hulikunte cross,
Gowribidanur Taluk, Chikkaballapura District, at that point of time the driver of the Tipper lorry bearing Reg.No.KA- 38-A-4858 drove it in a rash & negligent manner with high speed and dashed to rear side of the deceased motorcycle.
Due to the impact the deceased fell down on the road and sustained fatal injuries and died at the spot.
It is submitted that postmortem was conducted and corpse was handed over to the family members.
It is submitted that, prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy, he was an agriculturist and earning Rs.50,000/- p.m.
It is further submitted that because of death of deceased the petitioner has suffered both financially and emotionally.

It is contended that the accident happened because of rash and negligent driving of the driver of Tipper Lorry and as such both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Hence prayed to allow the petition.
3. Notice was duly served to respondent No.1, the respondent No.1 did not appear before this Tribunal.
Hence she was placed exparte.
4. After service of notice, the respondent No.2 appeared through its counsel & filed written statement by contending that the petition is not maintainable either law or on facts.
The respondent No.2 denied the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Tipper lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-38-A-4858.

However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms &
conditions of the policy.
The respondent denied the manner and involvement of the vehicle in the accident.
This respondent denied negligence on the part of the driver of Tipper lorry.
Per contra it is stated that the accident has taken place due to the negligence of the deceased.

Without prejudice to the above contentions it is averred that, the driver of the Tipper lorry did not possess valid &
effective DL at the time of the accident.
On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the policy by the insured, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Non- compliance of section's 134(c), 158(6), of MV Act is pleaded.
The petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties.
Rest of the petition averments are repudiated as false and baseless and it is prayed to dismiss the petition.
5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :

ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that she is the legal heir and dependent of the deceased ?
Bharathi vs The Kolluru Gurunath Construction ... on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14093335/
2 2) Whether the petitioner proves that the deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident that occurred on 27.08.2023 about 11.30 a.m,
near Hullikunte Cross, Gowribidanur - Gudibande, SH-94 road, Gowribidanur Taluk,
Chikkaballapura District, due to actionable negligence of the driver of Tipper lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-38-A-4858 ?

3) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed? If so, at what rate and from whom ?
4) What order or award ?
6. Petitioner examined herself as PW.1.
Ex's.P1 to 14 were marked on behalf of the petitioners.
The respondents did not choose to lead any evidence on their behalf.
7. Heard erudite counsel for the petitioner and respondent counsel on merits.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

8. This tribunal answers to the above issues are as follows :-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.4 : As per final order for the  following :
 REASONS 9. ISSUE NO.1 : The petitioner claims that petitioner is the wife of the deceased.

To prove the same,
petitioner filed affidavit-in-lieu of her chief-examination and deposed about the above relationship.
The Aadhar cards marked at Ex's.P.13 & 14 and contents of the police papers do fortify the said fact.
It is pertinent to note that this relationship of the petitioner with the deceased has not been disputed by the respondent No.2.

Since the evidence led by the claimants is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimant, this Tribunal hold that the petitioner is the legal representative of the deceased.
Therefore, claimant is the legal heir and dependent of deceased.
Hence, this Tribunal answers issue No.1 In the Affirmative.
10. ISSUE NO.2 :
The occurrence of the accident on the relevant date, time and place is not in dispute.
The parties are also not at variance with regard to the factum of the death of the deceased due to the injuries sustained in the said accident.
The conflict is with respect to actionable negligence.
The petitioner plead that the accident was caused due to the sole negligence of the driver of offending Tipper lorry.
Whereas the Insurance Company contends that the accident in question occurred because of negligence of the deceased.

sentences.text: Smt. Bharathi - the wife of deceased set the criminal law into the motion by lodging Ex.P.3-First information statement.

Based on the said FIS, the jurisdictional police registered FIR as per Ex.P.2,
investigated the matter and laid charge sheet (Ex.P.1) against the driver of Tipper lorry for the offences punishable under section's 279, 304(A) of IPC.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
Further more the careful perusal of Ex.P.4 and 6 being Spot Mahazar and Sketch it reflects that the accident happened on Gudibande - Gowiribidanur SH road.
On close perusal of the same it reflects that, the motorcycle in which the deceased was traveling was hit by the Tipper Lorry to its rear side.
It is further shows that the accident occured on the curve road.
If the driver of Tipper lorry was coming in a normal speed then he would certainly avoided the accident.
Above all even the charge sheet was also filed as against the driver of the offending Tipper lorry.
This court is aware of the fact that charge sheet is not a conclusive proof to come to conclusion with regard to rash and negligent act.
But having regard to the Ex.P.4 & 6 which were read in consonance with the Ex.P.1 Charge sheet it is crystal clear that there is an rash & negligent act of the driver of the Tipper lorry.
Another important aspects to be noted here is, respondent No.2 did not made any endevour to examine the driver of Tipper lorry.
Mere taking of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the testimony of other side, which has no sanctity in the eyes of Law.
Under such circumstances the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of Tipper lorry.
As such, this Tribunal answers issue No.2 In the Affirmative.
12. ISSUE NO.3:

The petitioner has produced the Aadhar card to show the age of the deceased as per Ex.P14 wherein the date of birth of deceased is shown as 01.01.1975, which indicates that he was aged (48 years 7 months 26 days) 49 years on the date of accident.

Therefore the appropriate multiplier as per Sarla Verma's case for the said age group is '13'.
13.
In this case the petitioner has claimed the compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- on the death of deceased in the road traffic accident.
The petitioner contended that, deceased was agriculturist and earning of Rs.50,000/-p.m.
To prove the income of the deceased, the petitioner has not produced any documents.
14. Be that as it may, in the absence of authentic proof of income of the deceased, this Tribunal has to consider his income notionally for calculating the compensation.
Admittedly the accident took place in the year 2023.
It is trite law that, when the petitioners have failed to prove the income, the income of the deceased has to be taken into consideration as notional income.
It is relevant to rely on the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered on Division Bench in the case of Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA.No.101144/2020 (MV) dated.05.07.2023.

"(b) The accident is of the year 2017.
The Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month as against the claim of Rs.2,50,000/- per annum.
To substantiate the said claim, the injured claimant has not placed any material on record, it is for the Courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.

sentences.text: notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant"
As such this court is taking the notional income as prescribed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.
Therefore in view of the above decision, the accident was occurred on 27.08.2023.
Therefore, Rs.16,000/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the deceased.

15. As per the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others), if the person died in the motor accident, the income with respect to the future prospect has to taken into consideration while awarding compensation.

entities.text: 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court has provide the chart for age of the deceased and percentage for future prospects in between below the age of 40 years 40%, 40 years to 50 years 25% and 50 to 60 years 25%.
The deceased is not a permanent Employee and not a fixed salary person and he died at the age of 49 years.
Therefore, in this case, 25% income has to be taken into consideration for future prospects.

Further as stated above that, as on the date of accident, deceased aged about 49 years and as such, 25% is added to the income of the deceased, then it comes to Rs.20,000/- p.m.
(Rs.16,000/- + 4,000/- i.e. 25%).
16.
The deceased died living behind one dependent.

As per principle laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarala Verma Case, 1/2 of his income is required to be deducted towards his personal expenses which comes to Rs.10,000/- p.m. (Rs.20,000 - Rs.10,000 = Rs.10,000/-).
17. The income of the deceased is taken as Rs.10,000/- p.m. and the multiplier '13' is applied, then the loss of dependency comes to Rs.15,60,000/- (Rs.10,000/- X 12 X 13).
Considering the above facts, I deem it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.15,60,000/- under the head of loss of dependency.

18. Further, as Law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, the compensation towards loss to estate, funeral expenses and consortium is to be awarded.

sentences.text: The petitioners contended that they have spent substantial amount towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies etc., but no documents are produced.

Hence this Tribunal award Rs.18,150/- towards loss to estate and Rs.18,150/- towards funeral expenses as enhanced at the rate of 10% on every 3 years and Rs.48,400/- towards consortium to the petitioner No.1.
By applying the observations made in the aforesaid case, as more than 6 years elapsed from the date of order amount of consortium, funeral expense and loss of estate to be enhanced.

REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.
21. It is contended in para 6 of the written statement that, respondent. No.2 has not issued any policy.

However careful perusal of policy and RTO records which is found in documents as per the contents of which the issuance of insurance policy is respect of Tipper Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-38-A-4858 and same is issued on 30.10.2022 and valid from 30.10.2022 to 29.10.2023,
covering the date of accident.
Hence, there is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondents No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% p.a.
from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within two months from the date of this order.

Hence issue No.3 is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
